currentUserGoal: Continue the ecosystem redesign with a real, expandable skill tree after the user correctly called the former Memory Nursery placeholder too basic and asked where the skill tree had gone.
workCompleted: Replaced the paged rectangular Memory Nursery offers with a dedicated 3600x1500 Memory Web containing 53 permanent-progression nodes.

Mapped the complete current progression model into the web: eight helper unlocks, four ranked helper tracks per helper, eight alternate modes, ten field-size memories, Broad Palm, Many Hands, and Field Embrace.
Arranged helper clusters around a horizontal production chain and added verified non-crossing branch geometry that can be extended into a much larger web.
Added compact overview icons, ranked pips, locked, ready, remembered, and selected node frames, colored branch connectors, and culling outside the visible tree viewport.
Added a large inspector card that follows hover selection and shows an enlarged animated icon, branch, explanation, current rank effect, cost, GT shortfall, and prerequisite text.
Added fit-to-world view, 1x through 8x zoom, cursor-centered mouse-wheel zoom, plus/minus controls, keyboard zoom, drag panning, and responsive desktop and phone layouts.
Wired every node directly to the existing permanent economy functions so displayed ownership, affordability, costs, rank effects, and purchases derive from the saved progression state.
Removed all obsolete offer-page state and hardened node dragging so a pan beginning on a purchasable node cannot accidentally buy it.
Added graph-contract tests for unique nodes, valid prerequisites and world bounds, and zero unrelated straight-line connector crossings.
verificationRun: npm run check passed: ESLint, 106 Vitest tests across 14 files, TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
Browser verification passed on the redesign route at 1280x720 desktop and 390x844 phone viewports.
A real Tiny Sprinkler node purchase deducted 5 GT, changed the node to remembered, illuminated its local branches, and updated the inspector.
Fit view, plus-button zoom, hover preview, enlarged-icon animation, drag panning, and Begin Next Run were exercised in the browser.
The active one-tile field still rendered correctly after leaving Memory Grove on phone.
No browser errors or warnings were reported during the final desktop and phone passes.

release.status: Local isolated prototype checkpoint; not merged into master or promoted to production.

currentGitStatus: Expected after checkpoint commit: the Memory Web files and this handoff are committed on codex/ecosystem-factory-prototype.
docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md appeared as an unrelated untracked file during the session and must remain untouched and uncommitted unless the user explicitly requests it.
The local Vite server remains available at http://127.0.0.1:5173.
knownIssues: This is an alpha structural and interaction pass, not the final Memory Grove art treatment.
Fit view intentionally makes all 53 nodes small enough to show the whole current web; players zoom for labels and use the inspector for readable detail.
The visible debugPanel overlay covers the bottom of the phone inspector because it is a developer-only route; the normal player route does not show that overlay.
The web currently represents the full implemented permanent model, but later recipes and systems will need new authored clusters and intermediary nodes.
Fresh-page loading starts a new active run when no active-field save exists, so browser testing the Game Over view after a reload requires the debug Force Game Over action or a natural failure.
nextRecommendedSteps: Hands-on test a real fresh run through Game Over and judge whether the Memory Web now feels like a rewarding destination rather than a placeholder menu.
Polish the first Tiny Sprinkler unlock and the transition back into Run 2 so the first remembered branch produces an immediate field payoff.
Add subtle grove ambience and cluster labels only after confirming the current zoom, pan, hover, and purchase ergonomics feel right.
Expand the web alongside new ecosystem recipes instead of inventing disconnected filler nodes before their gameplay exists.
doNotRevert: Keep the Memory Web data-driven and derive node state from the same permanent economy functions used by semantic controls.
Keep connector geometry non-crossing and extend the graph with tests when adding clusters.
Keep overview icons compact and move readable explanations into the animated inspector card.
Keep fit, zoom, pan, viewport culling, and phone composition as the foundation for the eventual large web.
Do not restore the old paged Memory Nursery offer buttons.
Do not treat these alpha visuals as final art and do not use the legacy 1200-tile harness as redesign evidence.
